name: Kindergarten
theme: God loves me and made me

units.title: God made everything
units.eq: Who made the world, and why?

lessons.title: God is our loving Father
lessons.idea: God is our Father. He is good, and he loves every one of us. He is always with us.
lessons.question: How do you know when someone loves you?
lessons.activity: Draw a picture of your family and trace a heart around it. Say, “God loves us.”
teach: Start with what children know: someone who feeds them, holds them and keeps them safe. “God is like that, only more” (CCC 239, 2779).
Jesus called God “Abba,” Father (Matthew 6:9). Say the Our Father’s first words slowly: “Our Father.”
Some children have a hard or absent father at home. Say “God is a loving Father” without comparing to anyone’s dad, and stay warm and simple.
talk: Who takes care of you at home?
What does your family do when someone is sad?
What would you like to tell God today?
quiz: Who is our Father in heaven?|God|A king far away|Nobody|A statue|0|God is our loving Father.
God loves…|Only good children|Only adults|Everyone|Only the strong|2|God loves every person.
lessons.life: At bedtime this week, say together: “God, thank you for loving us.”
lessons.saint: Thérèse of Lisieux: a little girl who loved God as her Father and trusted him in everything.
lessons.mem: God is my Father and he loves me.
lessons.hook: Hold a child’s picture of their own father or caregiver. Ask, “Who takes care of you?” Then say, “God takes care of you even more.”
lessons.assess: Ask each child to finish: “God is my Father, and he…”

lessons.title: God made the world
lessons.idea: God made the sky, the sea, the animals and the plants. He made them because he is good. He looked and said, “It is good.”
lessons.question: What is your favorite thing God made?
lessons.activity: Go on a short nature walk, or look at photographs. Each child names one thing God made and says “Thank you, God.”
teach: Genesis 1 shows God making everything one step at a time and calling it good (CCC 279, 299). Read it in short pieces.
Creation is a gift. We say thank you (before meals, on a walk).
Keep science separate and simple: “God made the world. Scientists find out how it works.”
talk: What did God make that you can see right now?
Why do you think God made so many animals?
How can we take care of what God made?
quiz: Who made the sky, sea and animals?|The wind|Nobody|People|God|3|God is the Creator.
What did God say about what he made?|It is bad|Nothing|It is boring|It is good|3|Genesis 1.
lessons.life: Take a walk with your family and say “thank you, God” for three things you see.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he called the sun, the moon and the animals his brothers and sisters because God made them all.
lessons.mem: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good. (Genesis 1:31)
lessons.hook: Bring a flower, a shell and a stone in a basket. Ask, “Who made these?” Let them hold each one.
lessons.assess: Ask each child to name one thing God made and say “Thank you, God.”

lessons.title: God made me
lessons.idea: God made me in a special way. I am a person, not a thing. God made me to know him and love him.
lessons.question: What can you do that animals cannot do?
lessons.activity: Trace each child’s hand on paper and write “God made me.” Display them together.
teach: Every child is made in God’s image, with a body and a soul (CCC 355–357). Say it plainly: “God wanted you.”
Psalm 139:13–14: “I praise you, for I am wonderfully made.” Teach one line.
Be sensitive to children with disabilities or hard stories. Everyone is wonderfully made.
talk: What are you good at?
What makes you different from your friend?
How can you show love to someone today?
quiz: Who made you?|A machine|The wind|God|Nobody|2|God made each person.
God made people to…|Be alone|Know him and love him|Fight|Be perfect|1|CCC 356.
lessons.life: Look in a mirror and say, “God made me and loves me.” Do it for five days.
lessons.saint: Bl. Carlo Acutis: a boy who loved God and computers and showed that everyone has gifts.
misc: “God made some people better than others.”
lessons.mem: I am wonderfully made. (Psalm 139:14)
lessons.hook: Let children look in a mirror. Say, “Who made that wonderful face? God did!”
lessons.assess: Ask each child, “Who made you?” and “Why?” (to know and love God).

lessons.title: Jesus is born
lessons.idea: God sent his Son, Jesus, to be a baby. Mary was his mother and Joseph took care of him. Jesus is God, and he is also a real person.
lessons.question: Who was in the stable with baby Jesus?
lessons.activity: Act out the story with a doll and a blanket. Sing a gentle Christmas song.
teach: Luke 2:1–20: Mary, Joseph, shepherds, angels, a manger. Tell it in four or five simple scenes (CCC 525–526).
Jesus is God’s Son who became a baby so we could know God (CCC 456).
Tell it gently and keep it real: Jesus was a real baby, not a toy or a myth. Sing a carol.
talk: How do we take care of a baby?
Who came to visit Jesus?
Why do you think God sent his Son as a baby?
quiz: Who was Jesus’s mother?|Elizabeth|Martha|Anna|Mary|3|Luke 2.
Where was Jesus born?|Bethlehem|Nazareth|Rome|Egypt|0|Luke 2:4-7.
lessons.life: Put a small crib scene where your family can see it and say “Welcome, Jesus” each night.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he made the first living nativity scene to help people see how Jesus was born.
lessons.mem: Today a Savior has been born for you. (Luke 2:11)
lessons.hook: Bring a doll wrapped in a blanket. Whisper, “A very special baby was born long ago.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who was born at Christmas? Who took care of him?”

lessons.title: Jesus loves children
lessons.idea: Jesus loved the children and held them in his arms. Jesus loves you right now.
lessons.question: How would it feel to sit on Jesus’ lap?
lessons.activity: Retell the story with felt pieces. Give each child a turn to say, “Jesus loves me.”
teach: Mark 10:13–16: the disciples tried to send the children away, but Jesus welcomed them (CCC 2785). Children are important to him.
Jesus’ love is for each one by name.
Let children sit on a lap or near you while you tell the story, to feel welcome.
talk: How did the children feel when Jesus hugged them?
What do you want to say to Jesus?
How can you be kind to the little children at your house?
quiz: What did Jesus do with the children?|Ignored them|Blessed them|Sent them away|Scolded them|1|Mark 10:16.
Jesus loves…|Only good children|Children too|Only grown-ups|Nobody|1|Jesus welcomes children.
lessons.life: Give someone at home a hug and say “Jesus loves you.”
lessons.saint: Bl. Laura Vicuña: a young girl who loved Jesus and prayed for her mother.
misc: “Only grown-ups can be close to God.”
lessons.mem: Let the children come to me. (Mark 10:14)
lessons.hook: Hold up a picture of Jesus with children. Ask, “How do you think the children felt?”
lessons.assess: Ask each child to say, “Jesus loves me.”

lessons.title: Jesus helps and heals
lessons.idea: Jesus helped people who were sick and sad. He still helps us today. We can ask him for help.
lessons.question: Who can we ask Jesus to help?
lessons.activity: Make “thank you” cards for a sick person. Pray together for them.
teach: Choose one simple story: Peter’s mother-in-law (Mark 1:29–31) or the ten lepers (Luke 17:11–19). Keep illness gentle (CCC 547–548).
Jesus still helps us today. We pray for the sick.
If a child has a sick loved one, say “We can pray for them” and avoid promises about healing.
talk: Who do you know who is sick?
How can we help them?
Why did only one man come back to say thank you?
quiz: Jesus helps people who are…|Strong|Sick and sad|Famous|Rich|1|Mark 1:29-34.
When Jesus helps us, we say…|Later|Thank you|Nothing|Go away|1|Luke 17:15-16.
lessons.life: Pray this week for someone who is sick, and make them a card.
lessons.saint: Damien of Molokai: a priest who cared for people with leprosy.
misc: “If I pray, everyone gets well right away.”
lessons.mem: Thank you, Jesus, for helping us.
lessons.hook: Put a bandage on a doll. Ask, “How do we help someone who’s hurt?” Then say, “Jesus helped people too.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to say one person they can pray for.

lessons.title: Mary is Jesus’ mother
lessons.idea: Mary said yes to God. She is Jesus’ mother and our mother too. She helps us love Jesus.
lessons.question: What do you do when your mom asks you to help?
lessons.activity: Say the first part of the Hail Mary together. Draw Mary and baby Jesus.
teach: Luke 1:26–38: the angel Gabriel asks Mary to be Jesus’ mother and she says yes (CCC 494–495). Keep it brief.
Mary is Jesus’ mother and our mother (John 19:26–27; CCC 963).
Teach the first line of the Hail Mary.
talk: What did Mary say to the angel?
When did you say “yes” to someone who asked for help?
What do you do when your mom asks you to help?
quiz: Who told Mary she would be Jesus’s mother?|A neighbor|A shepherd|An angel|A king|2|Luke 1:26-38.
What did Mary say to God?|Nothing|Yes|No|Maybe|1|Luke 1:38.
lessons.life: This week, when someone asks for help, say “Yes!” with a smile and think of Mary.
lessons.saint: Juan Diego: he said yes when Mary asked him to carry her message.
misc: “We pray to Mary instead of Jesus.”
lessons.mem: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
lessons.hook: Say, “Mary was a young girl who listened to an angel.” Hold up a picture of Mary.
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did Mary say to the angel?” (Yes).

lessons.title: The saints are God’s friends
lessons.idea: Saints are people who loved God very much. Now they are with God in heaven. They pray for us.
lessons.question: Who is your favorite saint?
lessons.activity: Show pictures of three saints. Match each saint to a fact about them.
teach: Saints are people who loved God very much and are now with him (CCC 828, 956). They pray for us.
Tell about one saint in a short story (Francis and the animals, Thérèse and little acts of love).
Say that saints were once children, too.
talk: Which saint is your favorite?
What can we do to be like the saints?
Why does Jesus want us to be friends with the saints?
quiz: Saints are…|Only old people|Strangers|God’s friends|Make-believe|2|Saints love God and are with him.
Saints pray for…|Nobody|Us|Only kings|Only priests|1|Hebrews 12:1.
lessons.life: Choose a saint for the year and put a picture where your family can see it.
lessons.saint: Nicholas: a kind bishop who gave gifts secretly to people in need.
lessons.mem: Saint (name), pray for us.
lessons.hook: Show photos of someone’s friend, then a picture of a saint. “Saints are God’s friends.”
lessons.assess: Ask each child to name a saint or one thing a saint did.

lessons.title: Angels help us
lessons.idea: Angels are God’s helpers. Each one of us has a guardian angel who watches over us.
lessons.question: When can you say thank you to your angel?
lessons.activity: Learn the Guardian Angel prayer with hand motions.
teach: Angels are God’s helpers, spirits without bodies (CCC 328–330). Each person has a guardian angel (CCC 336).
Psalm 91:11 and Matthew 18:10 support it.
Keep it comforting, not scary. Do not teach that angels are chubby babies.
talk: How could an angel help you?
When can we say thank you to our angels?
How is an angel like a helper at home?
quiz: Who is with us all the time to help?|A king|A monster|A cartoon|A guardian angel|3|CCC 336.
Angels serve…|Only kings|Pets|God|Nobody|2|Psalm 91:11.
lessons.life: Say the guardian angel prayer at bedtime this week.
lessons.saint: Padre Pio: he said, “Our guardian angel is always with us,” and asked people to send their angel.
misc: “My angel will get angry at me.”
lessons.mem: Angel of God, my guardian dear, to whom God’s love commits me here.
lessons.hook: Whisper, “Someone is always watching over you.” Reveal an angel picture.
lessons.assess: Ask children to say the first line of the prayer with you.

lessons.title: We belong to God’s family
lessons.idea: The Church is God’s family. We are baptized and belong to it. Our priest and our parish help us follow Jesus.
lessons.question: Who is in your family at church?
lessons.activity: Take a short walk around the church or look at photos. Name the people who help.
teach: The Church is God’s family, made up of the baptized (CCC 751, 1267). We meet at church and everywhere.
People help in the family: priest, deacon, teachers, parents.
Welcome children from different families.
talk: Who is in your church family?
Who helps us at church?
Why do we call it God’s family?
quiz: The Church is…|A game|A shop|God’s family|A zoo|2|CCC 751.
We join God’s family by…|Buying|Wishing|Baptism|Winning|2|CCC 1213.
lessons.life: Greet someone at church by name this week.
lessons.saint: Mother Teresa: she cared for people everyone else forgot, as a mother cares for her family.
lessons.mem: We are God’s family.
lessons.hook: Hold up a family photo. “This is my family. God has a family too: the Church.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who is in God’s family?” (Everyone who is baptized).

lessons.title: Our church building
lessons.idea: The church is God’s house. We are quiet and respectful there because Jesus is present. We find the altar, the cross and the tabernacle.
lessons.question: What helps us be quiet in church?
lessons.activity: Practice making the Sign of the Cross with holy water, genuflecting and sitting quietly.
teach: Teach the names by pointing: altar, cross, tabernacle with red candle, holy water font (CCC 1179–1186).
Practice quiet voices, walking feet, a reverent Sign of the Cross and genuflecting.
Explain that Jesus is truly there in the tabernacle.
talk: What do you see in our church?
Why do we make the Sign of the Cross?
How do we show respect for Jesus?
quiz: Where is Jesus kept in church?|In the tabernacle|At home|In a book|In the car|0|CCC 1379.
Holy water reminds us of…|A swimming pool|Our Baptism|Rain|A drink|1|CCC 1668.
lessons.life: Visit the church with a grown-up and look for the cross, the altar and the tabernacle.
lessons.saint: Tarcisius: a boy who carried Jesus in the Eucharist and protected him.
lessons.mem: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go to the house of the Lord.” (Psalm 122:1)
lessons.hook: Walk into the church quietly with the children. Whisper, “This is God’s house.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to point to the altar and tabernacle.

lessons.title: We go to Mass on Sunday
lessons.idea: On Sunday we go to Mass. We sing, listen, pray and thank God. It is the day of Jesus’ Resurrection.
lessons.question: Who do you go to church with?
lessons.activity: Make a “Sunday basket” of items you see at Mass. Name each one.
teach: Sunday is the Lord’s Day because Jesus rose on Sunday (CCC 2174). We go to Mass to listen, sing and thank God (CCC 2177).
Mass is a family meal of God’s family.
Do not shame children who miss Mass; invite and welcome.
talk: What do you like about Mass?
What do we do when we gather?
How do we get ready for Sunday?
quiz: On Sunday, Christians go to…|The mall|A race|Mass|Work|2|CCC 2177.
Sunday celebrates…|Nothing|A holiday for toys|A birthday|The day Jesus rose|3|CCC 1166.
lessons.life: Lay out your “Mass clothes” on Saturday night with your family.
lessons.saint: Bl. Imelda: a girl who loved Jesus in the Eucharist so much that she longed to receive him.
lessons.mem: This is the day the Lord has made. (Psalm 118:24)
lessons.hook: Ring a bell. Say, “It’s Sunday! What do you do on Sunday?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we do at Mass?”

lessons.title: Baptism makes us God’s children
lessons.idea: In Baptism, water is poured and God’s family welcomes us. We get a white garment and a candle. God’s life is in us.
lessons.question: What happens at a baptism?
lessons.activity: Look at a baptism candle. Each child blows out and re-lights a safe LED candle and says, “Jesus is my light.”
teach: In Baptism, water is poured with the words “I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit” (CCC 1213, 1239).
Signs: water, white garment, candle (CCC 1243). Show their baptismal candle if possible.
Baptism makes us God’s children and members of the Church.
talk: Do you know your baptism day?
What did they give you? (A white garment, a candle.)
Who are your godparents?
quiz: In Baptism we get…|A car|A cake|A new toy|Water and God’s life|3|CCC 1214-1216.
Baptism makes us…|Kings|Strangers|Soldiers|God’s children|3|CCC 1265.
lessons.life: Ask your parents to tell the story of your baptism day. Look at the photos.
lessons.saint: Lucy: a girl who stayed faithful to Christ; her name means light, like the baptismal candle.
lessons.mem: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.
lessons.hook: Pour a little water into a bowl and let children touch it. “Water gives life and cleans.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to show the Sign of the Cross.

lessons.title: The Eucharist is Jesus’ gift
lessons.idea: At Mass, bread and wine become Jesus. He gives himself to us. We prepare our hearts to receive him someday.
lessons.question: Why do we kneel at the consecration?
lessons.activity: Practice reverent hands and reverent posture. Draw an altar with a chalice.
teach: At Mass, the priest says Jesus’ words and bread and wine become his Body and Blood (CCC 1374). Speak reverently, not as a puzzle.
Children not yet receiving can still love Jesus: make a spiritual communion (“Jesus, I love you, come into my heart”).
Practice reverent hands and a respectful bow.
talk: How do we show love for Jesus at Mass?
What can you say to Jesus in your heart?
Why do we kneel?
quiz: At Mass, bread and wine become…|Water|A symbol only|Candy|Jesus|3|CCC 1376.
We show respect by…|Playing|Running|Being quiet and kind|Shouting|2|Reverence.
lessons.life: Make a quiet “thank you, Jesus” card to place in your Bible or prayer corner.
lessons.saint: Tarcisius: a young martyr of the Eucharist.
misc: “I am left out because I can’t receive.”
lessons.mem: Jesus, I love you. Come into my heart.
lessons.hook: Hold bread gently. “Bread helps us grow strong. At Mass, bread becomes Jesus.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who is in the Eucharist?” (Jesus).

lessons.title: God forgives
lessons.idea: When we do wrong, we can say sorry. God is always ready to forgive. He loves us even when we make mistakes.
lessons.question: What do we say when we are sorry?
lessons.activity: Role-play “I’m sorry. I forgive you.” Read a picture book about forgiveness.
teach: God always forgives when we are sorry (Luke 15:11–24; CCC 1422, 1439). Use the story of the lost sheep.
Practice “I’m sorry. I forgive you.”
Never use fear. Say, “God loves you even when you make mistakes.”
talk: What did you do when you hurt someone?
How did it feel when someone forgave you?
What does God do when we say sorry?
quiz: When we do wrong, God…|Is angry forever|Leaves|Forgets us|Is ready to forgive|3|CCC 1439.
We say…|“You’re wrong”|Nothing|“I’m sorry”|“Whatever”|2|Reconciliation.
lessons.life: This week say “I’m sorry” the moment you hurt someone.
lessons.saint: Maria Goretti: a girl who forgave as she was dying.
misc: “God is mad at me when I do wrong.”
lessons.mem: Jesus, I am sorry. Please forgive me.
lessons.hook: Tell about a child who broke a cup and hid. “How did he feel? What could he do?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we say when we hurt someone?”

units.title: Loving others
units.eq: How does Jesus want us to love?

lessons.title: Love God and love others
lessons.idea: Jesus said to love God and love our neighbor. We show love by being kind, sharing and helping.
lessons.question: How can you show love at home?
lessons.activity: Make a “kindness chain”: add a paper link for each kind act this week.
teach: Love God and love your neighbor (Mark 12:29–31; CCC 2055). Show love by sharing, helping, being kind.
Golden Rule in action: “Do to others what you want them to do to you.”
Praise real acts of kindness you notice.
talk: How do you like to be treated?
What is one kind thing you did today?
Who needs a friend at school?
quiz: The Golden Rule says…|Hide|Win|Treat others as you want to be treated|Be first|2|Matthew 7:12.
Jesus wants us to love…|Only family|Only ourselves|God and our neighbor|Only friends|2|Mark 12:30-31.
lessons.life: Do one kind thing a day this week; draw a heart each time.
lessons.saint: Martin de Porres: a Peruvian friar who loved the poor and animals.
lessons.mem: Love one another. (John 13:34)
lessons.hook: Hold a paper heart. “Jesus said the most important rule is love.”
lessons.assess: Ask each child to name one kind thing they will do.

lessons.title: Telling the truth
lessons.idea: God wants us to tell the truth. Lies hurt people. Telling the truth makes us feel free.
lessons.question: How does it feel when someone tells you the truth?
lessons.activity: Read a story where a character is honest. Act it out with puppets.
teach: God wants us to tell the truth (Exodus 20:16; John 8:32; CCC 2464, 2468). Truth makes us free.
Praise a child who tells the truth even when it is hard.
Model honesty yourself and avoid punishing honesty harshly.
talk: What does it feel like to tell the truth?
Who can you tell when you are afraid to tell the truth?
What does a lie do to a friendship?
quiz: God wants us to…|Hide things|Lie|Pretend|Tell the truth|3|Exodus 20:16.
When we tell the truth we feel…|Sick|Lost|Trapped|Free|3|John 8:32.
lessons.life: Choose one day this week for “truth day”: tell the truth no matter what.
lessons.saint: Thomas More: a man who told the truth even when it cost him.
misc: “Telling the truth always gets me in trouble.”
lessons.mem: The truth will set you free. (John 8:32)
lessons.hook: Show two faces, one hiding and one open. “Which feels freer?” Read a short story about honesty.
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we do when we have done something wrong?”

lessons.title: Saying sorry and forgiving
lessons.idea: When we hurt someone, we say sorry. When someone hurts us, we forgive. Jesus forgives us, so we can forgive too.
lessons.question: What can you do after you hurt a friend?
lessons.activity: Practice a sorry-and-forgive routine with a partner.
teach: When we hurt someone we say sorry; when someone hurts us, we forgive (Matthew 18:21–22; CCC 2843). Jesus forgives us first.
Forgiving means choosing to be kind, even if we still feel hurt.
Keep it safe: if someone is being hurt, tell a grown-up.
talk: When have you forgiven someone?
What do you say when you want to forgive?
Who forgives us always?
quiz: When someone says sorry, we can…|Hit|Ignore|Forgive|Tease|2|Matthew 18:21-22.
Jesus forgives us so we can…|Be mean|Keep score|Forgive others|Run away|2|Ephesians 4:32.
lessons.life: If someone upsets you this week, say “It’s okay. I forgive you.”
lessons.saint: Maria Goretti: she forgave her attacker with her last words.
misc: “If I forgive, I must play with them.”
lessons.mem: Forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us.
lessons.hook: Tear a paper heart and tape it. “It mends when we say sorry and forgive.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to act out “I’m sorry” and “I forgive you.”

units.title: Praying every day
units.eq: How do we talk to God?

lessons.title: We can talk to God
lessons.idea: Prayer is talking to God. We can pray with words, with songs or in quiet. God always listens.
lessons.question: When can you pray?
lessons.activity: Pray in silence for one minute, then a simple prayer: “Thank you, God. I love you.”
teach: Prayer is talking and listening to God (CCC 2559, 2565). Pray with words, songs or silence.
Matthew 6:6: pray in a quiet place. Practice a minute of quiet.
No “right” way for little ones: any loving words are prayer.
talk: What would you tell God today?
When is it easy to pray?
How do you feel when you pray?
quiz: Prayer is talking with…|The TV|The wall|A phone|God|3|CCC 2559.
We can pray…|Anywhere|Only at church|Only on Sunday|Never|0|1 Thessalonians 5:17.
lessons.life: Pick a time and place for a daily prayer with your family.
lessons.saint: Bernadette Soubirous: a girl who prayed the Rosary and saw Our Lady at Lourdes.
lessons.mem: Thank you, God. I love you.
lessons.hook: Hold a toy phone to your ear. “We can talk to God anywhere.”
lessons.assess: Ask each child to say a short prayer.

lessons.title: The Our Father
lessons.idea: Jesus taught his friends to pray the Our Father. We pray it every day.
lessons.question: Who do we pray to when we say “Our Father”?
lessons.activity: Learn the Our Father with hand motions, one line at a time.
teach: The Our Father is Jesus’ own prayer (Matthew 6:9–13; CCC 2759–2765). Teach it line by line with gestures.
Say it slowly. Explain a few words: “hallowed” (holy), “daily bread” (what we need).
Pray it every day at the same time.
talk: What do you ask for in the Our Father?
What does “daily bread” mean to you?
Who do you forgive?
quiz: Who taught us the Our Father?|A king|Jesus|A teacher|A saint|1|Matthew 6:9.
The Our Father begins with…|Glory be|Our Father, who art in heaven|Hail Mary|Lord, have mercy|1|CCC 2759.
lessons.life: Pray the Our Father before meals this week.
lessons.saint: Teresa of Avila: she taught that the Our Father is the best prayer to learn.
lessons.mem: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name.
lessons.hook: Say, “Jesus’ friends asked him, ‘Teach us to pray.’ He taught them a special prayer.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to say the first two lines with gestures.

lessons.title: The Sign of the Cross and Grace
lessons.idea: We begin and end prayer with the Sign of the Cross. We thank God before meals.
lessons.question: What do we say before a meal?
lessons.activity: Practice the Sign of the Cross slowly. Act out a family meal blessing.
teach: The Sign of the Cross is a short prayer of the Trinity (CCC 2157; Matthew 28:19). Trace it slowly forehead, chest, shoulders.
Grace before meals: thank God for food (CCC 2698).
Practice with a partner. Watch for left/right mix-ups.
talk: Why do we pray before eating?
What are you thankful for?
Who made the food?
quiz: We make the Sign of the Cross to…|Count|Scratch|Wave|Pray in the name of the Trinity|3|CCC 2157.
Before we eat we…|Run|Play|Thank God|Argue|2|Matthew 14:19.
lessons.life: Lead grace at one meal each day this week.
lessons.saint: Brother Lawrence: a kitchen worker who prayed while washing pots.
lessons.mem: Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive. Amen.
lessons.hook: Trace a big cross in the air. “This is how we start our prayers.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to make the Sign of the Cross and say grace.

units.title: Seasons of the Church
units.eq: How does the year help us follow Jesus?

lessons.title: Advent: waiting for Jesus
lessons.idea: Advent is a time to get ready for Christmas. We light candles on the Advent wreath and wait with joy.
lessons.question: Why do we light candles?
lessons.activity: Make a paper Advent wreath. Add a flame each week.
teach: Advent is the time to get ready for Christmas (CCC 524, 1163). Purple and pink candles on the wreath.
Light one more candle each week. Add acts of kindness.
Keep it joyful, not just “waiting.”
talk: What are we waiting for?
How can you get your heart ready?
What helps you wait?
quiz: Advent is a time to…|Go to the beach|Fast all day|Prepare for Jesus’s birth|Hunt eggs|2|CCC 524.
The candles of Advent are…|Yellow|Black|Green only|Purple and pink|3|Liturgy.
lessons.life: Light the Advent candle with your family each evening and say a prayer.
lessons.saint: John the Baptist: he told people to get ready for Jesus.
lessons.mem: Come, Lord Jesus.
lessons.hook: Light a purple candle. “We are waiting for something special.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we light in Advent? Why?”

lessons.title: Lent and Easter
lessons.idea: Lent is a time to pray and share. Easter is a time of joy because Jesus rose.
lessons.question: How can we share with others?
lessons.activity: Make a Lenten bank for the poor. Decorate an Easter egg with a cross.
teach: Lent: forty days of prayer, sharing and small sacrifices (CCC 1438). Easter: Jesus is alive! (CCC 540, 1169).
Alleluia returns at Easter.
Small promises that match a child’s age.
talk: What can you share this Lent?
Why do we celebrate at Easter?
How can you help someone in need?
quiz: Easter is when…|The Church began|Jesus was born|Jesus rose from the dead|The apostles were chosen|2|Luke 24.
In Lent we pray, fast and…|Buy toys|Sleep|Complain|Give to the poor|3|Matthew 6:1-18.
lessons.life: Put coins in a Lenten box for the poor each week.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he gave up everything to follow Jesus and care for the poor.
lessons.mem: Alleluia! Jesus is risen!
lessons.hook: Show a bare branch and a flower. “Lent is quiet. Easter is joyful.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we do in Lent? What do we say at Easter?”

lessons.title: Ordinary Time and Thank You
lessons.idea: Ordinary Time is the time of green, when we grow like plants in God’s love.
lessons.question: What helps a plant grow?
lessons.activity: Plant seeds in cups and watch them grow. Pray, “Help me grow, Lord.”
teach: Ordinary Time is green, the time of growing in God’s love (CCC 1163, 1168). Seeds and plants fit the parables.
Plant seeds and watch them grow.
Say thank you for the little things.
talk: What helps a plant grow?
What helps us grow in love?
What are you thankful for?
quiz: Green is the color of…|Easter|Ordinary Time|Lent|Advent|1|Liturgical colors.
We grow in love by…|Prayer and kindness|Fighting|Hiding|Winning|0|Colossians 3.
lessons.life: Water a plant with your family and thank God for the gift of life.
lessons.saint: Thérèse of Lisieux: she called herself a “little flower” and taught the little way of love.
lessons.mem: Thank you, God, for helping me grow.
lessons.hook: Show a green plant. “Green means growing.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What color is Ordinary Time? Why?”
